grade_rule: E3, grade_tag peer_reviewed. Experiment and simulation are filed separately. The simulation entries are claims about a MODEL of two-dimensional dipolar-repulsive particles in which a fraction of sites are spinners whose rotlet flow (cut off at 1.5 particle radii) adds transverse forces; the experiment entry is about charged PMMA spheres at an oil-water interface with magnetic spinners beneath them.

method_as_stated: SIMULATION: molecular dynamics in HOOMD-Blue v4.4.1 with custom plug-ins described only in the Supplementary Information; the pair potential mimics the coupling and forces between a spinner and its neighbour, the spinner flow being a rotlet cut off at r_c = 1.5a. Integrator, thermostat and time step are not stated in the file. Simulated systems hold roughly 1e5 to 1e6 particles; the orientational correlation exponent is fitted out to a quarter of the periodic box length. Performed by P. W. A. Schoenhoefer; scripts on request; simulation data at doi 10.7302/mvmb-3j46. EXPERIMENT: hydrophobic charged PMMA microspheres adsorbed at an oil-aqueous interface repel as permanent dipoles, U = A/r^3; a droplet about 1 cm across holds about 1e5 particles. Thermal melting is by density through Gamma = A (pi rho)^(3/2)/kT, the inverse dimensionless temperature. Driven melting: oleophobic magnetic TPM-haematite particles sit in the aqueous phase opposite PMMA sites and are spun by a rotating external field, their flows breaking detailed balance; the drive parameter Omega/Omega* is a ratio of hydrodynamic drag to dipolar force that includes the spinner fraction through a function derived in the SI. Experimental samples average about 1e3 to 1e4 particles. Data at doi 10.17605/OSF.IO/X4BRU.
not_entered: Defect densities, Gamma and Omega/Omega* at the transitions: figure-only (Figs. 2-5), so no transition location is entered as a number. The drive-parameter formula: part of it is defined only in the SI. The odd-to-conventional elastic constant ratio of about 1e-2: the authors call it a rough calculation and give it in the SI; in the note. The sheared-crystal comparison: in the SI and not claimed strongly by the authors.
note: The KTHNY exponents 1/4 (hexatic-fluid) and 1/3 (solid-hexatic) are theory values the paper tests against, not results of it; an entry uses 1/4 only because the paper reports its driven systems reaching it at the hexatic-fluid transition.
